annotations.name: female_exertional_angina_gate
annotations.hypothesis: Hypothesis: node 665 is a three-way AND gate that fires only for women (sex:0 set) with exercise-induced angina (exang:0 unset, i.e. exang=yes) and no left-ventricular hypertrophy on resting ECG (restecg:2 unset). The restecg:2 chain 2349 -> 2771 never leaves the ReLU linear region on standardized one-hot inputs (2349 in [1.15,3.11], 2771 in [1.99,3.72]), so the gate collapses exactly to relu(1.41 sex:0 - 1.71 exang:0 - 1.18 restecg:2 - 3.39). Evidence (train, n=242): pre-activation max is 2.117, reached only when all three conditions hold; removing any one condition drives it negative (no female: -0.86; no exang: -2.53; LVH present: -0.24). The gate is active on 8/242 rows (3.3%), always at the single value 2.117, and 7 of those 8 are positive cases. Closed form matches the forward pass (check_explanation closed-form err 0.0049, numeric err 0).

annotations.name: restecg2_relay_2447
annotations.hypothesis: Hypothesis: node 2447 is an always-active affine relay of restecg:2 (LVH on resting ECG). Evidence (train): pre-activation in [0.485, 2.516], so the ReLU never clips; through its 0.026 output weight it adds 0.026*1.02 = 0.026 per SD of restecg:2 to the logit (logit-term SD 0.026 vs total logit SD 4.3), i.e. it is practically inert and simply nudges the direct restecg:2 weight from 0.224 to 0.250. Closed-form err 0.0083 (3-s.f. rounding).

annotations.name: flat_slope_amplifier
annotations.hypothesis: Hypothesis: serial composition H(G(sex:0, exang:0, restecg:2), slope:2). Node 3598 = relu(1.51 slope:2 + 1.05 G - 0.76) and node 1650 = relu(1.29 G + 1.31*3598 - 0.73). Because G takes only the values 0 or 2.117 and slope:2 is binary, 1650 has exactly four regimes on train: G=0 & slope not flat -> 0 (n=131, 27% positive); G=0 & flat slope (slope:2) -> 0.446 (n=103, 63% positive); G on & slope not flat -> 2.097 (n=1, negative); G on & flat slope -> 6.092 (n=7, all positive). So without the gate it is a small additional flat-ST-slope bonus (+0.34 logit after the 0.772 output weight, on top of the direct slope:2 weight); with the gate it amplifies the female-exertional-angina signal, and the flat-slope ReLU 3598 makes the two conditions super-additive (6.09 vs 0.45+2.10). Evidence: activation_profile on node 1650 (train): active 45.9%, mean 0.375, SD 1.018, max 6.092; values confirmed by local forward pass.

records.narrative: Serial composition of the gate with a flat-slope ReLU.
Four discrete regimes; gate and flat slope combine super-additively.

annotations.name: heart_disease_logit
annotations.hypothesis: Hypothesis: additive composition. The logit z of node 0 is a linear score over 17 direct standardized inputs (dominated by ca 1.93, sex:1 1.67, cp:4 1.21, slope:2 1.05, chol 0.72, oldpeak 0.71) plus 0.772 x flat_slope_amplifier plus 0.026 x restecg2_relay; 7 inputs (trestbps, fbs:0, restecg:0, restecg:1, exang:1, thal:3, thal:4) are disconnected. get_formula shows node 0 as ReLU, but for this binary task the model output is sigmoid(z) on the pre-activation (compute_performance train AUC 0.945 equals AUC of z; sigmoid(relu(z)) would give 0.912). Evidence (train, n=242, local forward passes): direct-linear logit SD 4.33 vs amplifier term SD 0.79 vs relay term SD 0.026. Dropping the amplifier term lowers train AUC 0.945 -> 0.930 and accuracy 0.888 -> 0.868; the direct linear part alone gives AUC 0.931. So the network is essentially logistic regression plus one sparse nonlinear correction: a flat-slope bonus (+0.34 logit) and a large boost (+4.7 logit) for the 7 women with exertional angina, no LVH and flat ST slope. Kernel SHAP on the full model (train) ranks ca 0.149, sex:1 0.130, slope:2 0.121, cp:4 0.116, oldpeak 0.049, thal:7 0.046, chol 0.044 (mean |SHAP| on probability). Function preservation after the two input splits: max abs err 1.8e-15.

annotations.name: capital_gain_hinge
annotations.hypothesis: Capital-gain (standardised; output is P(income<=50K)) enters the logit as a convex piecewise-linear decreasing function: a direct linear term -2.658*cg (via idn_o63) plus a ReLU hinge -0.364*relu(1.161*cg-0.500) that steepens the slope from -2.66 to -3.08 above cg~0.43 SD (raw ~$4.3k; ~5.7% of rows). Large capital gains push strongly towards >50K. Evidence (train, 39,073 rows): closed form verified by get_formula; viz summaries confirm the exits; mean-ablating this leaf's logit contribution gives acc 0.8359 / AUC 0.8877 (baseline 0.8518 / 0.9056), mean |dP| 0.0624, max |dP| 0.997. Removing only the hinge (keeping the linear term) barely changes performance (AUC 0.9054): the capital-gain effect is mostly linear in the standardised value.

annotations.name: full_model
annotations.hypothesis: Root: P(income<=50K) = sigmoid(0.808 + linear_backbone + capital_gain_hinge + female_or_household_gate + 7 single-category offsets). Composition is purely additive in logit space; the children never feed each other. Category offsets (train logit deltas): unknown workclass +0.82, Without-pay +61 (override to <=50K, 17 rows), Exec-managerial -0.82, Wife -2.90, Japan +0.14 (two large near-cancelling terms), Separated +0.23, dead Private unit 0. Since every bump has a single binary input, each is exactly an affine function of that indicator; the network is therefore a logistic regression plus two genuine nonlinearities: a convex capital-gain hinge (slope -2.66 -> -3.08 above ~0.43 SD) and an OR-like ReLU gate that adds +0.58 logit for women and +2 to +3.6 logit for Priv-house-serv. 56 unconnected inputs are zero-effect entries. Evidence (train, 39,073 rows): acc 0.852, AUC 0.906. Mean-ablation AUC drops: linear_backbone 0.906->0.753, capital_gain_hinge ->0.888, wife_bump ->0.887, exec_managerial ->0.903, female gate ->0.904; others <0.001. SHAP (500 rows) top: relationship:0 Husband, education-num, capital-gain, Married-civ-spouse, Wife, Exec-managerial, age, hours-per-week, relationship:1, sex.

annotations.name: ischaemia_pathway
annotations.hypothesis: Serial composition of the ischaemia gate into a BP-adjusted gate and its readouts. (1) Gate 290 = ReLU(1.088*st_ischaemia_gate_bp - 0.817*trestbps + 0.151*cp:2 + 0.017*cp:3 + 0.046*thal:6 - 0.013*thal6_linear_passthrough - 0.485): it passes on the ischaemia evidence of 204_b, offset downward by resting blood pressure (high-BP patients need more ST-depression evidence to open it). (2) 1834 = ReLU(0.941*290 - 1.672): high-threshold amplifier, fires only when 290 > 1.78, making the pathway convex. (3) 1987 = ReLU(0.880*age - 1.585*290 + 0.179): an age term switched OFF by the gate, so age adds risk only for patients in whom 290 is quiet. Output contribution 0.135*290 + 0.165*1834 + 0.097*1987. EVIDENCE (train, n=242): 290 active 56% (100/135 of its active cases have 204 on; 35 open from low BP alone, mean predicted risk 0.13); 1834 active 26%, only when 204 and 290 are both on, and 78% of those patients are diseased; 1987 active in 64% of patients with 290 quiet vs 13% with 290 active. The thal:6 chain is functionally inert. Interpretation: the network has exactly one nonlinear mechanism - an ischaemia pathway that amplifies strong ST-depression/defect evidence and uses age as a fallback signal when that evidence is absent.

annotations.name: linear_indicator_ramp
annotations.hypothesis: A linear indicator ramp with an a5=1 veto. Evaluated per attribute value, the direct connections contribute: a1 = 1/2/3: +3.85/-2.84/-1.31; a2 = 1/other: +7.00/-3.54; a3 = 1/2: +3.93/-4.14; a4 = 1/2/3: +2.98/-0.63/-2.19; a6 = 1/2: +4.40/-4.63. So for a1,a2,a3,a4,a6 the first value raises the sum by 3.6 to 10.5 units, making the sum rise roughly linearly with the number of these indicators. Attribute a5 is inverted: a5 = 1/2/3/4 contributes -6.25/+2.51/+1.90/+1.90, i.e. a5=1 is an 8-unit penalty rather than a positive indicator. Together with the output bias (+1.855) the ramp crosses zero between one and two active indicators among {a1,a2,a3,a4,a6} when a5!=1, and an a5=1 pushes it back below zero. Evidence: the per-value contributions are exact (linear in the one-hot columns); sensitivity on train is largest for a2:1 (4.98), a3:1 (4.04), a6:2 (3.73), a5:1 (3.54), a1:2 (3.16). Note a5=1 acts as a veto, not an indicator.

annotations.name: two_of_five_with_a5_veto
annotations.hypothesis: The output composes the three children additively under the sigmoid: logit = 1.855 + Ramp - 7.413*Gate + 0.618*Chain. Ramp: the first value of a1,a2,a3,a4,a6 raises the sum (by 3.6-10.5 each), so with the bias it crosses zero between one and two active indicators among {a1=1,a2=1,a3=1,a4=1,a6=1} when a5!=1 (lower edge of a response peak); a5=1 instead costs about 8 logit units, pushing count-two cases below zero (an a5=1 veto). Gate: when three or more of the same five indicators are active it fires (pre-activation >=1.76) and its -7.41 readout overwhelms the Ramp (upper edge). Chain: +0.89 when a2!=1 and a5!=4; flips only 2 train predictions and is near-vestigial. Net: the model predicts positive approximately iff exactly two of {a1=1,a2=1,a3=1,a4=1,a6=1} hold AND a5!=1. Evidence (train, n=345): this rule agrees with the model on 331/345 rows (418/432 of all configurations); the 14 disagreements are near-boundary cases (|logit| < 1.8). Train accuracy 0.901, AUC 0.915; every train positive with a5=1 and exactly one other indicator (20 rows) is missed. Ablation: zeroing the gate drops train accuracy to 0.58; zeroing the chain gives 0.907. Inputs a2:2, a2:3, a4:2, a5:3 have no enabled edges and are zero-effect entries (sensitivity exactly 0).

annotations.name: two_of_five_peak
annotations.hypothesis: Two-of-five peak with an a5 handicap. The output is sigmoid(s) with s = -2.363 + Lin + Veto + 2.547*Gate - 0.599*A5 + 0.735*Inert, where Inert is identically 0. Lin (linear_first_value_score) rises by +4..+12 for each first value among a1, a2, a3, a4, a6 and is the rising edge: with at most one such first value s < 0 on all 432 configurations (max -0.42). Veto (atleast3_of_five_veto) is exactly 0 for at most two first values and <= -70 for three or more, so it is the falling edge: s < 0 for every configuration with three or more. Gate (a5_a3_bonus_gate) adds +8.5..+11 when a5 != 1 (more when a3 = 1) and nothing when a5 = 1 and a3 = 2; A5 is a -0.72 penalty for a5 in {2,4}. Net: with exactly two first values among {a1,a2,a3,a4,a6} the model predicts positive in 113 of 114 configurations when a5 != 1 but only 23 of 38 (61%) when a5 = 1 (the a5_a3 gate is weak or off there; pairs (2,3) and (3,4) always fail). So the network computes approximately 'exactly two of the five attributes a1,a2,a3,a4,a6 take their first value, and preferably a5 != 1': it agrees with [count5 == 2] on 96.3% of all 432 configurations and 95.9% of training rows, and reaches 88.7% train accuracy (AUC 0.925). Inputs a4:2, a5:2, a6:2 have no enabled connections and are zero-effect entries. Evidence: on train, ablating the veto drops accuracy 0.887 -> 0.562 and ablating the gate 0.887 -> 0.690; the score sign is negative for every configuration with <=1 or >=3 such first values. Comparison with the target rule (exactly two of all six attributes take their first value): the network has replaced a5=1 as a rule indicator with a5 != 1 as a bonus, so it is correct on two-of-six cases where a5 != 1 (113/114) but misses all 28 two-of-six cases in which a5 = 1 is one of the two, and wrongly accepts 23 of 38 three-of-six cases that include a5 = 1 (agreement with the rule 88.0% over all 432 configurations).

annotations.name: capital_gain_term
annotations.hypothesis: Hypothesis (supported): the full capital-gain contribution to the logit of P(income<=50K) (identity node cg_term collects the direct edge, relay 194 and hinges 1266/8342). It is a concave, monotonically decreasing piecewise-linear function of standardized capital-gain: slope -1.62 up to x=0.359 (~3.8k USD), -3.76 up to x=0.496 (~4.8k USD), then -5.83, because ReLU 1266 = relu(0.976x-0.35) and 8342 = relu(0.893*1266-0.12) switch on in sequence and both carry negative output weights. annotations.name: two_indicator_band
annotations.hypothesis: Output = sigmoid(Ramp - 1.20 - 5.64*Gate): an additive composition under the output sigmoid. Unconnected inputs a2:2, a4:2, a4:3, a5:2, a5:3 and a5:4 are zero-effect entries; the model never consults them. When no indicator is active the gate is about 13, and its -5.64 readout overwhelms the ramp (logit about -54). With one active indicator the gate still wins (logit <= -8.96). With two, the gate is (almost) off and the logit equals the ramp, -3.34 to +5.63. With three or more, the ramp itself is <= -3.41. So the network produces a peak at count two of the six rule indicators. The ramp makes the upper edge and the gate makes the lower edge: the mirror image of a single gate plus ramp construction. Because the ramp weights are uneven, the peak is not level. Pairs involving a6=1 (with a1, a2, a4 or a5) get logits -3.34 to -1.07 and fall below p=0.5, and so do some a2&a4 and a4&a5 configurations; a3&a6 stays positive because I3 is light. Train evidence (n=345): AUC 1.0, since every count-2 logit (>= -3.337) exceeds every other logit (<= -3.408), a margin of only 0.07. Accuracy at 0.5 is 0.890: 38 false negatives, all count-2 rows, and no false positives. Local ablation with the gate set to 0 drops train accuracy to 0.632 and turns every count<=1 row positive.

annotations.name: count_gate_a2_a3_a4_a6
annotations.hypothesis: A graded count gate over four of the six rule indicators. In indicator terms the pre-activation of 1158 is -13.56 + 8.28[a3=1] + 6.59[a2=1] + 5.58[a4=1] + 5.62[a6=1] - 1.68[a1=3] (a3 enters through its complement a3:2, weight -4.14). It fires iff at least three of {a2=1,a3=1,a4=1,a6=1} hold (activation >= 2.56) or a3=1 plus exactly one other with a1!=3 (activation only 0.30..1.31). a1=1 and a5=1 are not consulted. Readout -6.92, so the penalty to the output logit is graded: about -2.1 to -9.1 for the a3+one pairs, -17.7 to -86.6 for three or more. Evidence: closed form; train sensitivities (a3:2 1.44, a2:1 1.08, a6:1 0.98, a4:1 0.90, a1:3 0.27); exhaustive enumeration confirms the firing rule on 432/432 inputs. Role: the upper edge of the response peak (suppresses inputs with too many indicators), but the weak pair-level activation is not always enough to cancel the ramp (e.g. a1=1,a3=1,a6=1 stays positive).

With a5 in {3,4} the baseline logit is about -4.99; the ramp adds a1=1 +1.25, a2=1 +5.24, a3=1 +3.70, a4=1 +2.28, a6=1 +4.05, so it turns positive once about two strong indicators (a2,a3,a4,a6) are present (lower edge of a response peak). annotations.name: sex_exang_interaction
annotations.hypothesis: Hypothesis: a sex x exercise-angina interaction built from two chained ReLU gates. Gate 1213 = relu(1.23 sex:0 + 1.31 exang:0 - 0.509 cp:2 - 0.563 fbs:0 + 0.476 thal:7 + 0.091) is a female-without-exercise-angina score; gate 47 = relu(1.43 + 0.956 exang:0 - 1.93 h1213) fires for patients without exercise angina whose 1213 score is low (mostly men) and is shut off by 1213. The output reads -0.760 h1213 + 0.384 g47. Evidence (train, n=242): group mean block logit is +0.04 (male, exang), +0.18 (male, no exang), -0.39 (female, exang), -1.76 (female, no exang). Exercise angina has no direct edge to the output, so its entire effect is this block: flipping exang no->yes raises the logit by +1.81 on average for women (range 0.78..2.11) but by -0.17 for men (range -0.78..1.87). g47 is active for 84% of men without angina but 19% of women without angina. cp:2, fbs:0 and thal:7 only shift h1213 (sensitivities 0.22-0.26 vs 0.57-0.60 for sex:0/exang:0). Odd signs (thal:7 and fbs:1 making the block slightly less protective / more protective respectively) are small modifiers we do not interpret clinically. Ablating gate 47 to its mean drops train AUC 0.9457->0.9414; ablating 1213->output drops it to 0.9347.

annotations.name: capital_gain_effect
annotations.hypothesis: Capital-gain term (exit idn_capgain, added to the output logit): f = -2.49*cg - 2.32*relu(0.576*cg - 0.0522*nc32 - 0.274), inputs z-scored. For the 91.6% of train rows with zero capital gain (cg_z=-0.146) the gate is off and f=+0.36. The ReLU 1690 opens at cg_z=0.476 (5.2% of rows), steepening the slope from -2.49 to -3.83 per SD: a monotone one-knot piecewise-linear decrease in logit P(<=50K). annotations.name: income_logit_root
annotations.hypothesis: ROOT (supported). Output 0 = sigmoid(z), z = 1.399 + 48 direct input terms + 12 hidden readouts (9 child annotations); 52 of the 107 one-hot/standardized inputs are unconnected and listed here as zero-effect entries. Class 1 is the 76% majority (presumably <=50K), so negative weights push toward high income. The model is essentially a sparse logistic regression with one consequential nonlinearity. Direct edges carry logit SD 3.37 of 3.85 (mean-ablating them drops train AUC 0.910->0.518); all hidden readouts together carry SD 1.32 and mean-ablating every hidden unit costs only acc 0.856->0.838, AUC 0.910->0.895. The only nonlinearity that matters is age_late_career_hinge (4647): keeping it alone recovers acc 0.850 / AUC 0.904. It turns the direct age slope (-0.88) into a U-shaped age effect with its minimum at age z~0.8. The other children are lookups or affine relays: capital_gain_affine_relay steepens the capital-gain slope to -2.54/SD; relationship1_indicator (-1.03 for relationship:1), occupation0_country0_gate (+0.92 for occupation:0 unless native-country:0), occupation8_relays (+0.45) and occupation1_relays (+0.37) are category offsets; country32_affine_relay and the native-country:4 part of the age hinge memorise rare countries; occupation6_relationship1_gate is near-inert (<=0.10 logit); dead_relationship_chain (613->2245->8678->170) and node 2114 are identically 0 on every valid input. Children combine ADDITIVELY in the logit (each child exit has one readout edge into node 0; no child feeds another). annotations.hypothesis: Node 791 = ReLU(0.325 + 1.084*sex:0 - 0.218*sex:1 + 2.200*exang:0), read out with -0.452. Since sex and exang are one-hot binaries it takes only three values on train: 0 for all patients with exercise-induced angina (n=82, disease rate 0.73), 0.959 for men without it (n=96) and 3.702 for women without it (n=64). annotations.name: fbs_normal_fixed_defect_gate
annotations.hypothesis: Node 2034 = ReLU(-1.027 + 1.156*fbs:0 + 1.016*thal:6), read out with -0.942. An AND gate: it is 3.386 only for patients with a fixed thallium defect (thal:6) AND normal fasting blood sugar (n=10 on train), 0.018 for fixed-defect patients with high sugar (n=5), and 0 for everyone else (93.8%). It subtracts 3.19 logits for that small group. Evidence suggests it is a training-set correction rather than a clinical rule: among the 10, the linear core over-predicted 4 of 5 negatives as positive; the gate moves all 5 negatives below 0 while the 5 positives stay above 0. This is the only thal:6 pathway and the only fbs:0 pathway. Mean-ablation drops train AUC 0.9437 -> 0.9388 and accuracy 0.888 -> 0.872 (largest single-gate effect), but it rests on 10 patients, so treat it as likely overfitted.

annotations.name: thal6_fixed_defect_gate
annotations.hypothesis: Fixed-thallium-defect correction gate. 2065 = ReLU(0.795*thal:6 - 0.885*fbs:1 - 0.719) on z-scored one-hots is a discrete indicator: 0 unless thal:6=1 (fixed defect), 2.727 if additionally fasting blood sugar is normal, 0.148 if fbs>120. It enters the logit with weight -1.117 (-3.05) and, via identity_707, adds 2.178*2065 to the thalach gate 707 (a further ~-0.52 through 3677). Its role is to cancel the linear core's over-prediction of disease for thal:6 patients with normal FBS (the linear core gives them +0.60 through the thal:3 edge and other terms). EVIDENCE: TRAIN n=242: 2065 is exactly 0 for all thal:6=0 patients (227/242). thal:6=1 & fbs:1=0 (n=10): 2065=2.727; thal:6=1 & fbs:1=1 (n=5): 2065=0.148. Active 6.2%. Sensitivity (mean |grad|): fbs:1 0.055, thal:6 0.049. Readout: direct -1.117*2065 => logit -3.05 for fixed-defect/normal-FBS patients; via identity_707 -> 707 -> 3677 a further ~-0.52. Mean-ablating 2065 lowers train AUC 0.9424 -> 0.9363 and acc 0.884 -> 0.872. On the 10 thal:6&normal-FBS patients (disease rate 0.5) the linear core alone gives mean logit +3.78 (9/10 predicted diseased; thal:6 patients get +0.60 from the negative thal:3 edge); with the gate the mean logit is +0.25 and all 10 are classified correctly. Thus it is a learned correction for a 10-patient subgroup the linear core over-calls (likely partly fitted to train noise).

annotations.name: exertional_ischaemia_hinge
annotations.hypothesis: EXERTIONAL-ISCHAEMIA HINGE. Node 855 = ReLU(1.055*trestbps + 0.896*oldpeak + 0.850*exang:1 - 1.358*cp:1 - 0.937*slope:1 - 0.802) is a sparse ischaemia score: high resting BP, ST depression and exercise-induced angina push it up; typical angina (cp:1) and upsloping ST (slope:1) push it down. Node 1501 = ReLU(0.393 - 1.428*855) is its clipped complement. Read out together (+1.300*855 + 0.814*1501) they form a hinge: contribution = 0.320 + 0.138*855 while 855 < 0.276, and 1.300*855 above. So below threshold these five features have almost no effect (effective slopes ~0.12-0.19), and above it they act with full weight (trestbps +1.37, oldpeak +1.17, exang:1 +1.11, slope:1 -1.22, cp:1 -1.77 per SD). EVIDENCE (train, n=242): 855 active 36% (mean 0.75, max 7.9); 1501 saturated at 0.393 whenever 855=0; mean 855 is 0.23 without vs 1.78 with exercise angina; positive rate 80% when 855 active vs 24% when zero. Sensitivity of 855: cp:1 0.49, trestbps 0.38, slope:1 0.34, oldpeak 0.32, exang:1 0.31. Ablation (local, readout replaced by train mean): AUC 0.947->0.926, accuracy 0.897->0.847, the largest nonlinear effect in the network.

annotations.name: age_noangina_cp4_chain

Serial ReLU chain: 1958 = ReLU(1.049*age + 0.061) passes age above about the mean; 1669 = ReLU(1.104*1958 + 1.460*exang:0 - 0.916) is active exactly when there is NO exercise-induced angina (100% of exang:0 cases, 0% otherwise) and grows with age; 3353 = ReLU(1.089*1669 + 0.813*cp:4 - 0.234) adds asymptomatic chest pain. It is read out with -0.515, so it LOWERS risk. Effect: (1) for cp:4 patients (always active) it trims the direct +1.213 cp:4 weight to a net +0.79; (2) for older patients without exertional angina it subtracts up to ~0.65 per SD of age, reversing the small direct +0.236 age effect in that subgroup, and adds ~-0.82 per SD on exang:0. Reading: an asymptomatic-chest-pain patient who is older but does NOT get angina on exercise is less likely diseased than cp:4 alone suggests. annotations.name: st_depression_gate
annotations.hypothesis: Hypothesis: hidden gate 557 = ReLU(1.283*oldpeak + 0.559*thal:7 - 1.076*slope:3 - 0.417*fbs:0 + 0.085) is a one-sided ischaemia-evidence detector. It switches on mainly with exercise-induced ST depression (oldpeak), more readily when there is a reversible thal defect (thal:7), is pushed down by a downsloping ST segment (slope:3, which is clinically counter-intuitive; it is rare, 7%, and the direct linear core has no slope:3 term, so this is probably how the network absorbs slope:3 at all), and slightly by normal fasting sugar (fbs:0). It enters the logit with weight +0.746, so it only ever adds risk. Evidence (train, n=242): closed form exact (single ReLU); active on 47.9% of patients (83% with thal:7, 27% without); max 4.72, logit contribution SD 0.78; sensitivity oldpeak 0.62 > slope:3 0.52 > thal:7 0.27 > fbs:0 0.20; replacing it by its mean drops train AUC of the logit from 0.947 to 0.938, the largest of the three gates.

annotations.name: female_exang_and_gate
annotations.hypothesis: Hypothesis: hidden gate 1239 = ReLU(0.571*sex:0 + 0.903*exang:1 - 0.853) is a Boolean AND of female sex (sex:0) and exercise-induced angina (exang:1). Evidence (train, n=242): truth table of the standardised one-hot inputs gives activation 1.199 for women with exang (n=19, positive rate 63%) and exactly 0 for the other three cells (male/no exang n=96 pos 40%; male/exang n=63 pos 76%; female/no exang n=64 pos 14%; the male+exang pre-activation is -0.004, just below the threshold). Weighted +1.730 into the logit it adds +2.07, which cancels most of the direct female protective term (-1.573*sex:0 contributes -2.18 for women vs +1.14 for men): the network learns that exercise angina erases the female advantage. Active on 7.9% of patients, logit contribution SD 0.56; mean-ablation drops train AUC 0.947 -> 0.940. Closed form exact.

annotations.name: thalach_cp3_protective_gate
annotations.hypothesis: Hypothesis: a protective high-exercise-capacity gate. Serial chain thal:3 -> 3818 -> 2124. 3818 = ReLU(1.003*thal:3 - 0.192) is a normal-thallium indicator taking only the values 0 (abnormal thal) and 0.702 (normal thal, 56% of patients). 2124 = ReLU(1.338*thalach + 0.763*cp:3 - 0.108*3818 - 0.932) fires when maximum heart rate is high, much more readily with non-anginal chest pain (cp:3): active on 80% of cp:3 patients but 10.5% of others (30.6% overall, max 2.88). It enters the logit with weight -0.918, so it only ever lowers risk, adding a hinge to the direct linear thalach (-0.470) and cp:3 (-0.743) terms. The thal:3 branch only moves the threshold by -0.076 (sensitivity 0.025 vs thalach 0.41, cp:3 0.23) and is nearly inert. Evidence (train, n=242): closed form exact; logit contribution SD 0.49; mean-ablation drops train AUC only 0.947 -> 0.945, the weakest of the three gates.

annotations.name: heart_disease_logit
annotations.hypothesis: Root hypothesis: an additive composition that is essentially logistic regression plus three one-sided ReLU corrections. Logit z = -0.680 + LINEAR CORE + 0.746*st_depression_gate + 1.730*female_exang_and_gate - 0.918*thalach_cp3_protective_gate, and the prediction is sigmoid(z) (get_formula renders the output as ReLU, but for this binary task the model applies a sigmoid to the output pre-activation). LINEAR CORE = 19 direct input->output edges, dominated by ca (+2.607, number of vessels), sex:0 (-1.573, women lower risk), chol (+0.870), slope:1 (-0.833, upsloping ST protective), cp:1 (-0.785), slope:2 (+0.743), cp:3 (-0.743), fbs:0 (+0.627), trestbps (+0.519), thal:7 (+0.490), thalach (-0.470), sex:1 (+0.390), thal:4 (+0.383), thal:6 (-0.351), cp:4 (+0.312); age, restecg:0, exang:0/1 near zero. cp:2, fbs:1, restecg:1, restecg:2 are unused. Corrections: (a) ischaemia evidence (ST depression, reversible thal defect) adds risk; (b) women with exercise angina lose most of their sex protection (AND gate, +2.07 logit); (c) high max heart rate, especially with non-anginal pain, removes extra risk. Evidence (train, n=242): accuracy 0.876, AUC 0.947. Linear core logit SD 4.90 vs gates 0.78 / 0.56 / 0.49. Linear core alone AUC 0.930; mean-ablating each gate gives AUC 0.938 / 0.940 / 0.945, so together the nonlinear parts add ~+0.017 train AUC. SHAP (probability scale): ca 0.170 >> sex:0 0.080 > slope:1 0.063 > cp:3 0.058 > slope:2 0.053 > thal:7 0.050 > chol 0.038 > thalach 0.034 > oldpeak 0.029. Function preservation of the refactored model 1.8e-15; all leaf closed forms exact up to 3-s.f. display rounding (max 0.027).

annotations.name: count_gate_3of4
annotations.hypothesis: An at-least-three-of-four first-value detector over attributes a2, a3, a4, a6 (a1 and a5 are not consulted, apart from a weak a5=4 term). In indicator terms the pre-activation is -24.87 + 11.00*I(a2=1) + 10.13*I(a3=1) + 11.97*I(a4=1) + 10.64*I(a6=1) + 2.43*I(a5=4) (a3 and a6 enter through their complements a3:2, a6:2 with negative weights). Its -6.04 readout then drives the output logit far negative.

annotations.name: a5_veto_count_peak_model
annotations.hypothesis: Additive composition under the output sigmoid: logit = -0.213 + Linear + 3.945*A4gate - 6.037*Count3of4 - 0.578*A1unit - 0.370*A2chain, i.e. in indicator terms Linear + 9.54 I(a4!=2) - 6.04 G - 1.62 I(a1=2) + 0.022 I(a2=3) - 0.57, with G the at-least-three-of-{a2=1,a3=1,a4=1,a6=1} gate. Mechanism: (1) Count3of4 is a veto: whenever k4 = #{a2=1,a3=1,a4=1,a6=1} >= 3 it subtracts at least 41.7 logits and the model predicts class 0 (0/84 configs positive). (2) Otherwise the sign is set by the linear score plus the a4!=2 bonus: a5=1 contributes about -17 relative to the other a5 values and vetoes almost everything (1/87 a5=1 configs with k4<3 positive); with a5!=1, k4=0 is mostly negative (6/36 positive) and k4 in {1,2} is almost always positive (211/225). So the network approximates 'a5 != 1 AND one or two of {a2,a3,a4,a6} take their first value' (agreement 95.1% over all 432 configurations, 94.8% of train rows). a1:1 (node -1) has no enabled edges and is a zero-effect entry; a1 matters only through the direct a1:2/a1:3 terms and the affine a1:2 unit. The two minor children are linear/near-constant corrections (mean-ablation changes 3.2% and 0.3% of train predictions); the count gate is the dominant nonlinearity (mean-ablation flips 52%). EVIDENCE: composed closed form (sigmoid of the weighted sum of children); exhaustive enumeration over 432 configurations; train performance of the composed model accuracy 0.655, AUC 0.766 (identical to the evolved network). Relative to the MONK-2 target (exactly two of six first values), the network ignores a1=1, treats a5=1 as a veto instead of a counted indicator, and counts only a2,a3,a4,a6, so it fires for one OR two first values among those four.

annotations.name: age_effect
annotations.hypothesis: Age shape function: identity_age = 0.179 age_z - 0.423 age_gate(age_z) = 0.179 age_z - 0.423 relu(1.045 age_z - 0.478). This is an inverted-U in the logit: it rises with age to a peak near 59 years (+0.05), then falls (-0.09 at 65, -0.24 at 70, -0.44 at 77; -0.39 at 35). So the model treats middle-to-late-50s as the riskiest age and gives the oldest patients a lower risk than the direct slope alone would. This is an evolved non-monotone age effect, a small one. annotations.name: heart_disease_logit
annotations.hypothesis: Root: z = -0.054 + linear_core + age_effect + bp_slope_effect + chest_pain_effect + thal_effect, and P(disease) = sigmoid(z). get_formula shows the output as ReLU, but the evaluator applies a sigmoid to the pre-activation for binary classification. The composition is purely additive, so the model is a generalised additive logistic model: one linear backbone over 11 features plus four per-feature-group shape functions (age inverted-U, saturating BP with an upsloping-ST discount, a per-category chest-pain lookup, and an additive thallium term). Unused inputs: sex:0, fbs:1, restecg:1, thal:7 (mostly redundant one-hot complements; thal:7 acts as the reference via thal:3/thal:6). Only two pieces are materially nonlinear: the age hinge (1499) and the BP/slope:1 hinge (3392). The cp:2 and thal:4 gates are exactly affine on the binary data, and the cp:3 x slope:3 gate is near-inert. Replacing all five hidden gates with affine fits moves the logit by SD 0.16 and train AUC 0.9407 -> 0.9384, with identical accuracy (0.876). annotations.name: capital_gain_hinge
annotations.hypothesis: Capital-gain (standardised) enters the logit as a convex decreasing piecewise-linear function y = -2.01*cg - 2.61*relu(0.770*cg - 0.409) (exit idn_cg feeds output with weight 1). Slope is -2.0 below cg = 0.531 SD and -4.0 above; 4.8% of rows are above the kink. Large capital gains drive P(<=50K) to ~0. Evidence (train split, 39,073 rows; output is P(income<=50K); baseline acc 0.8542 / AUC 0.9108): closed form from get_formula; line_plot summary: train contribution ranges -51.9 to +0.29, correlation with cg -0.997 (monotone). Local mean-ablation of this leaf: acc 0.8445, AUC 0.9047, mean|dP| 0.057, max|dP| 0.998.

annotations.name: capgain_marital_gate
annotations.hypothesis: Gate leaf (exit idn_gate). Main term 2.413*h1013 with h1013 = relu(1.473 - 0.438*NeverMarried + 0.619*Honduras - 1.17*relu(0.682*cg - 0.35)); plus 0.254*relu(0.176 + 0.845*NeverMarried) (unit 3583), plus Honduras' direct +1.88, plus a negligible chain 0.039*relu(-0.272 + 0.988*relu(-0.267 - 0.426*Cambodia + 0.512*h1013)). Behaviour: a constant offset towards <=50K of +4.25 logit for non-never-married rows and +2.34 for never-married rows (1013 shrinks more than 3583 grows), which a second capital-gain hinge (unit 1594, kink at cg 0.51 SD) removes as capital gain rises; the offset is gone above cg 2.74 SD (0.7% of rows). So capital gain also acts by cancelling a baseline offset, and its effect is larger for non-never-married people. Honduras (14 rows) gets +183 logit (forced to <=50K, fitted to 14 rows). Combined with the linear backbone's marital weights, the net marital effect is: Married-civ-spouse ~3 logit lower than Divorced/Never-married/Separated/Spouse-absent; Widowed in between. Evidence (train split, 39,073 rows; output is P(income<=50K); baseline acc 0.8542 / AUC 0.9108): sensitivity summary: |dy/dx| cg 0.08, NeverMarried 0.98, Honduras 3.37, Cambodia 0.011 (Cambodia path is negligible). Local mean-ablation: acc 0.8402, AUC 0.9055, mean|dP| 0.068.

annotations.name: age_youth_gate
annotations.hypothesis: Exit idn_youth = 1.416*relu(-0.820 - 1.096*age - 2.108*OtherService) - 0.041*age + 0.374*OtherService (age, OtherService standardised). For Other-service workers the ReLU is dead and they get a flat +1.1 regardless of age: Other-service and youth are substitutes (OR-like), not additive. annotations.name: few_indicators_gate
annotations.hypothesis: An at-most-one-of-six detector (lower edge of the peak). ReLU unit 773 = relu(-3.54 a1:1 - 4.17 a2:1 - 4.41 a3:1 - 2.27 a4:1 - 3.72 a5:1 - 4.16 a6:1 + 1.52 a4:2 - 0.07 a1:2 + 0.21 a5:3 - 4.47) on z-scored inputs. In indicator terms its pre-activation is about +12 to +16 when no attribute takes its first value, and each first-value indicator subtracts 4.9-8.8. Evidence (train, n=345, full sample): active on 19/19 count-0 and 70/70 count-1 rows, on only 7/113 count-2 rows (pairs a1&a4 and one a1&a6, activation <= 0.52) and on 0/143 rows with count >= 3. Its -7.61 readout drives low-count logits to between -99 and -12. Alone it ranks the classes with AUC 0.67.

records.narrative: Closed form (sympy, 3 s.f.). Each first-value indicator lowers the pre-activation by 4.9-8.8 from a base of ~12-16, so the unit is on for counts 0-1 and off for counts >= 3.

Train split, full sample (local forward pass on read-only code + get_viz_summary sensitivity). Gate active on every count-0/1 row, 7/113 count-2 rows with small activation (<=0.52, i.e. <=4 logit units after the -7.61 readout), never for count >= 3.

annotations.name: descending_count_ramp
annotations.hypothesis: A linear ramp that falls with the number of first-value indicators (upper edge of the peak). The ten direct input->output edges give each attribute's first value a contribution 7-12 lower than its other values (a1 -10.2, a2 -8.2 vs a2=2 / -11.9 vs a2=3, a3 -12.1, a4 -7.6/-6.9, a5 -10.0, a6 -12.2). Evidence (train, full sample): ramp + output bias lies in [21.3, 25.7] at count 0, [8.6, 18.2] at count 1, [-3.5, 7.9] at count 2 and below -3.7 for every count >= 3 row, so it crosses zero between two and three indicators. Weights are not uniform: a3 and a6 (binary attributes) carry the largest drops, so count-2 rows involving a3 or a6 sit closest to zero. Alone it ranks poorly (AUC 0.62) because counts 0-1 score highest.

records.narrative: Closed form. Every attribute's first value contributes 7-12 less than its other values, so the ramp falls linearly with the count of first-value indicators.

Train split, full sample. Ramp+bias is positive on all count 0-1 rows, mostly positive on count-2 rows and negative on every count >= 3 row. Alone it ranks poorly (AUC 0.62) because count 0-1 rows score highest.

annotations.name: two_indicator_peak
annotations.hypothesis: Output = sigmoid(Ramp - 7.61 * Gate - 0.93): an additive composition in logit space. The descending ramp makes counts >= 3 negative; the at-most-one gate overrides the ramp's high values at counts 0-1. The logit therefore peaks at exactly two first-value indicators. Inputs a1:3, a2:2, a3:2, a5:2, a5:4 have no enabled connections and are zero-effect entries. Evidence (train, full sample): AUC 1.0 - every count-2 row outranks every other row - but the margin is thin (min positive logit -3.52 vs max negative -3.75), and the threshold is miscalibrated: only 86/113 count-2 rows exceed 0.5 (accuracy 0.922); the misses are pairs involving a3/a6/a5/a1 where the ramp's heavier weights push the logit below zero. No count != 2 row is predicted positive.

Train split, full sample. Logit peaks at count two; all count-2 rows outrank all other rows (AUC 1.0) but with a thin 0.23-logit margin, and 27/113 count-2 rows (mostly pairs involving a3 or a6, whose ramp weights are largest) fall below 0.5, giving accuracy 0.922.

annotations.name: bp_gated_ischaemia_amplifier
annotations.hypothesis: Serial gate plus amplifier on ischaemia evidence. (1) Gate: 290 = relu(0.944*ischaemia_score - 1.44*high_bp_gate - 0.897): passes only strong ischaemia evidence (204 > 0.95) not cancelled by high resting BP; active in 71/242 train rows, of which 79% have disease (30% when off). (2) Amplifier: 5615 = 0.248 + 0.998*290 (always active, affine), 2335 = relu(0.893 + 0.898*290 - 1.02*high_bp_gate) (off only for high BP, 27 rows), and 1834 = relu(-1.96 + 0.81*290 + 0.85*2335 + 0.86*5615 + 0.69*fbs:1). With 2335 active and normal fbs, 1834 = relu(2.44*290 - 1.26 - 0.86*high_bp_gate), i.e. threshold 290 > ~0.52; with high fbs the threshold drops below 0 so 1834 is on even when 290 is off (20 rows, at most +0.57 logit). Fitted on train rows with both active: 1834 = 2.40*290 - 1.11. (3) Readout: logit += -0.062*204 + 0.439*290 + 0.747*1834, which on train is about 2.14*290 - 0.81 (resid SD 0.52) when 290 is active and 0.04 +/- 0.17 when off. So the pathway is effectively one steep hinge: risk logit rises ~2 per unit of BP-discounted ischaemia above threshold. annotations.name: flat_slope_amplifier
annotations.hypothesis: Two serial ReLUs turn flat ST slope and the angina gate g=665 into a large risk term. In indicator units 3598 = relu(-2.298 + 3.098[flat slope] + 1.288 g) and 1650 = relu(-0.359 - 1.286[asymptomatic cp:4] + 1.944[thal=4] + 1.683*3598). So with flat slope, 1650 = relu(0.988 + 2.168 g) if chest pain is not asymptomatic and relu(-0.298 + 2.168 g) if it is: a flat-slope bonus of 0.99 (logit +1.42) that is withheld for asymptomatic patients (who already get +2.06 from the linear term), plus a slope-gated amplification of the gate (logit +3.1 per unit g). Without flat slope 3598 needs g > 1.78, so 1650 is almost always 0. The thal=4 flag 2011 passes through to the output. EVIDENCE (train, n=242, full sample): 1650 by (flat slope, asymptomatic cp:4, gate fires): (1,0,0) n=42 constant 0.990 (38% positive); (1,1,0) n=40 always 0 (80% positive, already high from linear cp:4 +2.06); (1,0,1) n=4 mean 2.57 (4/4 positive); (1,1,1) n=24 mean 2.71, max 7.59 (83% positive); no flat slope: 0 on 131/132 rows. Removing 1650 entirely: train AUC 0.953 -> 0.919, acc 0.893 -> 0.831; mean logit contribution on gate rows +2.84.

annotations.name: older_normal_fbs_age_hinge
annotations.hypothesis: Serial composition of ca_relay and normal_thal_flag into an age hinge for patients with normal fasting blood sugar. 2034 switches on above an age threshold that depends on thal (fixed defect: always; reversible defect: ~+0.3 SD; normal: ~+0.8 SD) and drops with ca; it never fires when fbs>120. Once on it subtracts 1.39 logit per age SD, reversing the direct age slope (+0.56) to -0.82, i.e. among older, normal-sugar, abnormal-thal patients the model predicts slightly less risk with age, matching a negative age-outcome correlation in that train subgroup (r=-0.12, n=82). Modest effect (AUC 0.9605->0.9484 when mean-ablated); plausibly a fit to this subgroup rather than a clinical mechanism. Evidence (train, n=242): 2034 = relu(-1.014 + 0.944 age + 1.407 fbs:0 + 0.793 thal:6 + 0.906*ca_relay - 0.578*normal_thal_flag), read out -1.469. Train: active 82/242; 0/33 with fbs>120. Age-SD thresholds (fbs normal, ca=0): normal thal +0.83, reversible defect +0.31, fixed defect -3.2 (always on); each ca level lowers the threshold ~0.2 SD. Past the hinge, logit slope in age = 0.563 (direct) - 1.469*0.944 = -0.82/SD. Empirically corr(age, y) is -0.12 among the 82 active rows vs +0.23 among inactive rows, consistent with the reversal. annotations.name: heart_disease_logit
annotations.hypothesis: Additive composition at the logit: a 15-term linear model plus four hidden corrections, then sigmoid. Unlike a plain logistic regression, thal has no direct edge: it acts only through thal_defect_oldpeak (abnormal thal: +3 logit and steep oldpeak slope) and the age hinge. no_angina_bp_gate subtracts risk without exercise angina and makes BP matter only with it. older_normal_fbs_age_hinge flattens/reverses the age effect for older normal-sugar patients with abnormal thal. ca_relay is an affine boost to the ca weight. Hidden units carry substantial signal: mean-ablating all of them drops train AUC from 0.960 to 0.870. cp:2, restecg:0, restecg:2 and thal:7 are unconnected, zero-effect entries. Evidence (train, n=242): Root logit = -0.586 + direct linear terms (SD 2.84) + 1.658*ca_relay (SD 0.48) - 0.678*no_angina_bp_gate (SD 1.21) + 1.749*thal_defect_oldpeak (SD 2.38) - 1.469*older_normal_fbs_age_hinge (SD 1.09); total logit SD 4.61. Largest direct weights (per SD): ca 1.33, slope:2 1.08, trestbps 0.84, sex:1 0.71, fbs:1 -0.68, chol 0.62, cp:3 -0.59, age 0.56. annotations.hypothesis:
Customer-service-calls threshold. identity_csc = 1.635*CSC (direct edge); 1255 = relu(0.003 - 2.878*state37 + 0.129*dayMinutes - 0.595*CSC) read out with weight 2.598, cancelling the CSC slope while 1255 is on (0-2 calls) and releasing it from 3-4 calls on. Net: flat logit for 0-2 calls, then ~+1.25 logit per extra call. State 37 rows switch 1255 off.

Evidence (train, n=4000): Customer-service-calls threshold. Logit term = 1.635*CSC + 2.598*relu(0.0033 - 0.595*CSC + 0.129*dayMinutes - 2.878*state37). For CSC 0-2 the relu is on in 95-98% of rows and cancels the slope (net 1.635-2.598*0.595 = +0.09/sd): mean term 0.94, 1.04, 1.11 for 0, 1, 2 calls. From 3 calls the relu shuts off (on in 3% at 3 calls, 0% at 4+): mean term 1.79, 3.04, 4.30, 5.55 for 3-6 calls, about +1.25 logit per call. Train churn by calls: 0-3 ~0.11, 4: 0.44, 5: 0.57, 6: 0.68, so the network places the threshold at 3-4 calls. A linear model cannot do this (linear R2 of the term 0.73). State 37 (84 rows, z=6.83) drives the relu negative, so for those rows CSC is linear throughout: logit effect of being in state 37 runs from -2.0 (0 calls) to +0.97 (3+ calls). Train AUC: mean-ablation 0.898 -> 0.819; replacing the term by its best linear fit 0.898 -> 0.879.

annotations.name: heavy_usage_and_service_tradeoff
annotations.hypothesis: Heavy-usage detector with a service-call bump that heavy usage switches off. 7701 = relu(1.23*dayCharge + 1.46*eveMinutes - 0.506); 5611 = relu(0.60*dayCharge + 0.69*7701 + 0.01*state:40 - 0.763) = relu(1.45*dayCharge + 1.01*eveMinutes - 1.11) when 7701 is on; readout +1.30. So churn rises steeply (about 1.9 logit per SD of day charge) once combined day+evening usage is high: 5611 is on for 27% of rows (churn 27% vs 9%); mean contribution +1.69 logit at 250-300 day minutes and +3.48 above 300. 10992 = relu(0.68*custServCalls - 1.48*5611 - 0.585), readout +1.22: extra churn from customer-service calls (on for 73-100% of rows with 3+ calls; +0.63 logit at 4 calls, +1.9 at 6), cancelled when 5611 is large (heavy users who call are not penalised again). The state:40 weight (0.01) is negligible. Note: after z-scoring, totalDayCharge and totalDayMinutes are the same column (charge is an exact multiple of minutes), so the network uses them interchangeably. Evidence (train, 4,000 rows): closed form from get_formula (3 s.f. display matches exit activations to 0.0121); viz summary attached; local mean-ablation of this part's logit contribution gives AUC 0.878 (baseline 0.908), logit SD 0.863; replacing it by its best linear fit on its inputs gives AUC 0.896.

annotations.name: usage_service_nonlinear
annotations.hypothesis: Additive sum (identity node nl_agg, weight 1) of the five leaves on the continuous usage and service-call inputs. The leaves never feed each other; they are summed in logit. Together they encode the classic churn rules: churn rises sharply with heavy day+evening usage (heavy_usage, day_charge_no_voicemail, day_minutes_hinge) and with 4+ customer-service calls (service_calls_hinge), especially when day usage is low (service_calls_low_day_usage), while heavy users are not penalised again for calls (10992). This block is where the network beats logistic regression: replacing each leaf by its least-squares linear fit on its own entry inputs lowers train AUC from 0.908 to 0.836 (L2 logistic regression on all 71 inputs: 0.843). Shapley split of that 0.072 AUC: heavy_usage_and_service_tradeoff 0.029, service_calls_low_day_usage 0.018, day_charge_no_voicemail 0.016, service_calls_hinge 0.007, day_minutes_hinge 0.002. Evidence (train, 4,000 rows): closed form from get_formula; viz summary attached; local mean-ablation of this part's logit contribution gives AUC 0.709 (baseline 0.908), logit SD 1.541; replacing it by its best linear fit on its inputs gives AUC 0.836.

annotations.name: full_model
annotations.hypothesis: Root: P(churn) = sigmoid(-1.729 + linear_backbone + state_offsets + usage_service_nonlinear + minor_hinges), additive in logit; the four children never feed each other. 26 unconnected inputs (24 state one-hots, areaCode:510, totalEveCalls, totalEveCharge, totalIntlMinutes, totalIntlCalls and others) are zero-effect entries. Interpretation: a logistic-regression backbone (international plan +, voicemail plan -, intl charge +, night minutes +), a per-state offset table (exactly linear in the one-hots), and a block of genuine ReLU hinges on day/evening usage and customer-service calls that implements the known churn rules (heavy day usage without voicemail; 4+ service calls, especially with low day usage). Evidence (train, 4,000 rows): AUC 0.908, acc 0.909. Mean-ablation AUC: linear_backbone -> 0.826, usage_service_nonlinear -> 0.709, state_offsets -> 0.902, minor_hinges -> 0.908. Replacing every hidden unit by its least-squares linear fit on its own inputs gives AUC 0.836 (L2 logistic regression on all 71 inputs: 0.843), so essentially all of the gain over a linear model comes from usage_service_nonlinear (Shapley share: heavy usage/service tradeoff 0.029, service calls with low day usage 0.018, day charge without voicemail 0.016, service-call hinge 0.007, day-minutes hinge 0.002). Rare-category effects (net logit, train rows): state:11 -2.14 (73 rows, 3 churners; empirical log-odds offset -1.20), state:4 +2.02 (41 rows; empirical +0.83), state:47 +1.17 (72), state:26 +0.92 (75), state:0 -0.76 (56), state:22 suppresses the low-usage service-call unit (in-state effect -1.97 to +0.98). These are 1.5-2.5x the empirical offsets: candidates for repair. SHAP (300 rows) top: day charge, customer-service calls, international plan, voicemail plan, eve minutes, day minutes (the same column as day charge after z-scoring), intl charge, night minutes, vmail messages, account length.

annotations.name: csc_usage_gate
annotations.hypothesis: Hypothesis: a low-usage hinge whose threshold rises with customer service calls (CSC). 807 = relu(-1.36 dayMin + 0.05 CSC + 0.69*2627 + 0.61*2796 - 1.30), where 2627 = 1.01 + 0.32 relu(0.87 CSC - 0.09) (always positive, affine in a CSC hinge) and 2796 = relu(0.41 - 1.00 eveCharge + 0.37 CSC + 0.15 state:41 + 0.34*12926), with 12926/13061 a two-stage CSC hinge that turns on at 3 calls. 1264 = relu(0.077 - 0.32 intlCharge + 0.39*807) adds 0.39*807 and a convex low-intl-charge hinge. Readout 1.59*807 + 1.81*1264 (252 is near dead, readout -2e-5, and holds a state:2/state:44/state:4 path). Evidence (train, n=4000): sensitivity of 807 is dayMin 0.63, eveCharge 0.22, CSC 0.20. Mean gate logit rises 1.1 -> 7.4 from 0 to 7 calls. With the backbone +2.02 dayMin, the logit is V-shaped in day minutes; for CSC>=4 the low-usage arm dominates (empirical churn 0.88 low-day vs 0.24 high-day, which the network reproduces). The same hinge also lifts low-CSC, very-low-day customers (93 rows, predicted 0.17 vs empirical 0.04): a mild overextension. totalEveCharge equals totalEveMinutes after z-scoring, so the gate effectively uses evening usage. Ablation: linearising this gate drops train AUC 0.901 -> 0.851; restoring it alone on the fully linearised model gives 0.836 -> 0.899. It is the source of nearly all of the network s gain over a linear model.

annotations.name: day_charge_step_state0
annotations.hypothesis: 6792 = relu(0.98*state:30 - 1.63*dayCharge - 0.17) is a falling ramp in day charge; 4785 = relu(0.70*state:0 - 0.81*state:30 - 1.13*6792 + 1.14), readout -0.24. Outside states 0 and 30 this is a small saturating step: 0 below about 130 day minutes, -0.27 logit above about 180 minutes (it slightly offsets the day-usage hinges). In state:0 (56 rows) 4785 rises to about 7 and gives -1.6 logit; in state:30 (74 rows) it is always 0 (+0.2 relative). Note: after z-scoring, totalDayCharge and totalDayMinutes are identical columns (charge is an exact multiple of minutes), as are totalEveCharge and totalEveMinutes, so the network uses them interchangeably. Evidence (train): closed form and table attached. Linearising it does not lower AUC (0.9107 vs 0.9102); restoring it alone adds 0.005. Mainly a state:0 offset plus a small step.

annotations.name: csc_zero_calls_bump
annotations.hypothesis: Two single-input units on customer-service calls. 3237 = relu(-0.67*CSC - 0.64) is on only for customers with 0 calls (readout +1.09, value 0.21: +0.23 logit); 4279 = relu(0.28*CSC + 0.83) is always on, so with readout -0.25 it is linear, -0.054 logit per call. Together they bend the backbone's +0.64-per-call CSC slope slightly: 0 calls get +0.23 logit relative to a straight line. Any function of a discrete input with few values is a lookup table; this one is nearly linear. Evidence (train): closed form and table attached. Linear fit R2 0.80; linearising changes AUC by -0.0003; restoring alone adds 0.002. Nearly negligible.

annotations.name: state_offsets
annotations.hypothesis: Hidden units fed only by state one-hots. The categories are mutually exclusive, so the block is exactly a per-state logit offset table. 2016 = relu(1.69 - 1.61*state:31) is on outside state 31 and off inside it; with readout -1.31 it gives state:31 +2.47 logit, which cancels most of the backbone's direct state:31 term (-2.0): net +0.76 (90 rows). 10379 = relu(0.92*state:46 - 1.53*state:0 - 0.35*state:22 - 0.94) is on only in state:46: -1.14 logit there (net with backbone -2.43, 80 rows, 5 churners). 11068 (state:50, -0.39), 15556 (state:15, +0.27) and 16346 (state:40, +0.38) are single-state offsets. state:0 and state:22 only push 10379 further below zero (no effect). Evidence (train): closed form attached; linear least-squares fit on the one-hots is exact (R2 1.0), so it is functionally linear. Mean-ablating it lowers train AUC 0.910 -> 0.903: a 0.007 train-AUC gain from per-state offsets on 55-90 rows each, likely overfit (the warranted offsets from observed churn rates are about half the fitted ones).

annotations.name: churn_model
annotations.hypothesis: Root: P(churn) = sigmoid(-1.258 + linear_backbone + service_calls_low_day_usage + day_charge_no_voicemail + heavy_day_eve_usage + day_charge_step_state0 + csc_zero_calls_bump + state_offsets), additive in logit; the seven children never feed each other. 25 unconnected inputs are zero-effect entries. Performance sources (train, local): full AUC 0.910; all nonlinear children replaced by least-squares linear fits 0.834 (jointly 0.833; refit L2 logistic regression 0.843). The 0.077 gain over linear comes from three hinges: day_charge_no_voicemail (restored alone +0.054, Shapley 0.031), service_calls_low_day_usage (+0.038, Shapley 0.022) and heavy_day_eve_usage (+0.038, Shapley 0.021); the two day-usage hinges overlap, so their gains are sub-additive. State one-hots act as fixed per-state offsets (direct weights and single-state units), plus three switches inside the service-call gate (state:43 off, state:0 and state:35 on).

annotations.name: csc_low_day_gate
annotations.hypothesis: Hypothesis (supported): customer-service-calls x low-day-usage interaction. 104 = relu(0.576 + 0.755 CSC + 1.309 relu(0.332 CSC - 0.212) - 0.862 dayCharge - 1.939 relu(1.429 dayCharge + 1.216) + 0.206 state30 + 0.006 state6 + 1.688 h2039), read out 0.617*h104 + 0.688*relu(0.980 h104 - 0.618). Logit grows ~0.7-1.4 per service call and falls with day charge (slope -3.6 per z while 4834 is on), reaching zero above the day-charge median. Evidence (train, 4000 rows): mean contribution 1.13 (0 calls) to 6.97 (6 calls) in the lowest day-charge decile, 0 above p50 for <=4 calls; active on 32% of rows; sensitivity dominated by dayCharge (0.64) and CSC (0.29). For low-call, low-usage customers it cancels the negative part of the linear dayMinutes slope (+1.105 per z), so day usage below p75 has an almost flat net effect. Side inputs: state30 shifts 104 (row effect -0.85..+1.13, mean -0.15 net of its direct edge); 2039 (state9-gated) is active on only 3 train rows (CSC 8-9). Linearising this child alone costs 0.012 train AUC; restoring it alone to the all-linear model gains 0.050.

annotations.name: csc_threshold_low_day

Evidence (train): +0.35 constant for 0-2 calls; from 3 calls it adds ~+1.3 logit per extra call when day charge is below its median, much less in p50-75 and nothing above p75 (except 7+ calls). Active on 12.8% of rows. Together with csc_low_day_gate the model matches the empirical pattern: CSC>=4 & day charge <p25 churn 0.90-1.00 (model 0.81-0.84); CSC>=4 & day charge >p50 churn 0.19-0.20 (model 0.20-0.25); CSC 0-3 churn 0.04-0.06 below p75 (model 0.05-0.07). The two gates are largely redundant: linearising either alone costs only 0.012-0.013 AUC, both together 0.063.

annotations.name: full_model
annotations.hypothesis: Hypothesis (supported): P(churn) = sigmoid(-2.455 + linear_backbone + csc_low_day_gate + csc_threshold_low_day + day_minutes_hinge + account_length_hinge + state20_switch + minor_state_units + dead_state_chain); all children combine additively in the output logit; the 27 unconnected inputs (incl. totalEveCharge, totalIntlCharge, areaCode 408/510, 23 states) have zero effect. annotations.hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: a two-stage hinge on total usage (day+evening+night) that raises churn steeply for heavy users WITHOUT a voice-mail plan, with a state:25 switch that disables the second stage. 3460 = relu(0.615*dayMin + 0.535*dayCharge + 0.653*eveCharge + 0.365*nightMin - 0.99*voiceMailPlan - 1.83) (dayMin==dayCharge after z-scoring, so the day weight is effectively 1.15); output +3.12. 4045 = relu(0.81*dayCharge + 1.45*3460 - 1.62*6037 - 0.905), output +2.55. 6037 = relu(0.47 + 1.13*state:25) is always on; it is a constant except on state:25 rows, where it subtracts ~13 from 4045's pre-activation. EVIDENCE (train, n=4000): closed form (max err 0.009). 3460 on 522 rows (churn 49% vs 9%), 4045 on 381 rows (64% vs 9%). Leaf logit contribution by usage score (1.15*day+0.65*eve+0.37*night) without a voice-mail plan: [1.5,2) +2.3 / churn 28%; [2,2.5) +5.8 / 93%; >=2.5 +12.6 / 100%; with a plan the same scores give <=+0.7 and churn 5-9%. state:25 gate: only 3 training rows (all churners) are heavy enough to be affected, logit -5.8 (pred 0.98 -> 0.82): a rare-state switch that is wrong on train. Linearising this leaf costs 0.046 train AUC; restoring it alone onto the fully linearised model gains 0.078: the largest single source of nonlinear performance.

annotations.name: csc_usage_gate
annotations.hypothesis: Low-usage x customer-service-calls gate. Node 807 = relu(-1.2 - 1.39 dayMin + 0.87*h2627 + 0.72*h2796 ...) is a hinge that is ON for low day minutes; its knot moves up with service calls (CSC enters via 13061->12926->2796 and 9555->2627) and with low eve charge / low night minutes (2796, 12926) and voicemail plan (9555). 1264 = relu(0.12 - 0.31 intlCharge + 0.43*807) amplifies 807, more for low international charge. Readout 1.68*807 + 1.92*1264 (+0.38*12809, which is dead: 12809 = relu(-0.78 - 0.54*h2796) is 0 on every row since h2796 >= 0). Its mean slope in day minutes (-2.31/z) cancels the backbone's +2.75/z, so the network's logit is V-shaped in day minutes, with the low-usage arm raised by about +1.8, +4.5, +6 logits at CSC = 4, 5, 6 relative to CSC <= 3. Evidence (train): gate logit by CSC x dayMin bins rises with CSC (CSC0 lowest-usage bin 8.64, CSC4 12.85, CSC6 13.22) and falls with dayMin; full-model partial dependence over dayMin is V-shaped with the low arm lifted by CSC (min logit -3.85 at CSC0, -1.50 at CSC4, +1.31 at CSC6). Empirical churn for CSC>=4 is 1.00/0.96/0.86 in the three lowest dayMin bins vs ~0.05 for CSC<4, matching. Performance: linearising this child alone drops AUC 0.908 -> 0.839; restoring it alone onto the fully linearised model gives 0.905 of the 0.908. It also contains a rare-category switch: state:20 (82 rows) zeroes node 2796, removing the CSC/eve-charge path (logit effects -5.1 to +1.1 per row).

annotations.name: churnModel
annotations.hypothesis:
Root: P(churn) = sigmoid(-2.009 + usageResponse + intlPlanSwitch + usageHinges + stateUnits + areaCodeUnits + accountLengthUnits + linearBackbone). annotations.name: day_eve_cascade
annotations.hypothesis:
Day x eve bill interaction. 103 = relu(1.554 eveCharge + 0.928) (off below eve charge ~14.5) is read out at -0.717 and passed through the near-identity relu chain 5908 -> 10233 into 9165 = relu(0.609 dayCharge + 0.484*10233 - 0.770*14599 - 0.982), read out at +2.713. Net: at low day charge the cascade cancels the backbone eve-charge slope (down to -2.2 logit), at high day charge it adds up to +2.5 logit when eve charge is also high, i.e. churn rises with the combined day+eve bill. 14599 = relu(0.884 CSC - 0.848) (on from 3 service calls) switches the bill hinge off for complaining customers, so bill and CSC effects do not stack.

EVIDENCE (train, n=4000, local ablation): full AUC 0.9243 (L2 logistic regression 0.8433). All nonlinear children jointly replaced by least-squares linear fits on their own inputs: 0.8333; all hidden mean-ablated: 0.659. The 0.091 nonlinear gain comes from two children: heavyUsageNoVmail (restore alone +0.0708, Shapley 0.057) and serviceCalls (+0.0489, Shapley 0.035); restoring both gives 0.9244 (= full). intlChargeHinges, stateUnits and accountLengthHinge contribute nothing over their linear fits. The model is miscalibrated on train (mean p 0.336 vs base rate 0.1415; global shift -1.875 needed). Rare-category effects are constant offsets: state:11 -2.18, state:46 -1.63, state:4 +1.12 (mixed direct/hidden, range -0.53..+1.48), state:47 +0.92, state:39 -0.86, state:31 +0.70, state:45 off-switch of the call veto.

annotations.name: heavy_day_eve_usage
annotations.hypothesis: Hinge on combined day+evening usage, read out twice. 1694 = relu(1.127*dayMinutes + 0.763*eveCharge - 0.009*state:27 + 0.012*28715 - 1.121) (z-scored), readout +2.03; 3237 = relu(0.871*1694 - 0.478), readout +1.05, makes the hinge steeper (convex) once 1694 exceeds 0.55. 28715 = relu(0.811 + 1.234*state:35 + 1.001*11600) and 11600 = relu(1.011*state:20 - 2.214) are state dribbles whose effect through the 0.012 weight is under 0.11 logit; state:27 shifts the threshold by at most -0.2 logit. Mean contribution is 0 unless both day and evening usage are well above average: +1.2 logit at 200-220 day and 250-300 eve minutes, +2.6 at 220-250/250-300, +4.3 at 250-280/250-300, +6.6 at 280+/250-300 and +8.3 when day > 280 and eve > 300 (train churn 60-72% in the heavy cells, vs 3-12% below 200 day minutes). Note: after z-scoring, totalDayCharge and totalDayMinutes are identical columns (charge is an exact multiple of minutes), as are totalEveCharge and totalEveMinutes, so the network uses them interchangeably. Evidence (train, local forward passes): replacing this child's logit contribution by its least-squares linear fit on its entries changes train AUC 0.9193 -> 0.9131 (linear-fit R^2 0.40); restoring it alone onto the fully linearised model (AUC 0.8303) gives 0.8749 (gain +0.045). Closed form from get_formula; sensitivity summary attached.

annotations.name: usage_brake
annotations.hypothesis: Two usage signals feeding the service-call gate 997. 4397 = relu(0.653*dayCharge + 1.327*15054 + 0.578*23191 - 0.804*20866 - 0.502), with 15054 = relu(1.483*dayCharge + 0.998*eveCharge + 1.089) and 23191 = relu(1.007*dayCharge - 1.567): a convex, increasing ramp in day charge (and to a lesser extent evening charge), zero only for low-usage customers; it enters 997 with weight -1.718, i.e. it is a brake that shuts the gate for heavy users. 20866 = relu(1.01*state:35 - 0.317) is on only in state:35 (value 6.45) and removes the brake there (4397 in-state mean 0.15 vs 1.77): a rare-state switch. 1694_b is the split copy of the heavy-usage hinge 1694 (same function as in heavy_day_eve_usage) entering 997 with weight +0.206. Note: after z-scoring, totalDayCharge and totalDayMinutes are identical columns (charge is an exact multiple of minutes), as are totalEveCharge and totalEveMinutes, so the network uses them interchangeably.

annotations.name: state_offsets

annotations.name: service_call_gate
annotations.hypothesis: Many customer-service calls AND low usage -> churn. 997 = relu(0.389*CSC + 0.494*csc_escalation.7689 - 1.718*usage_brake.4397 + 0.206*usage_brake.1694_b - 0.641), readout +3.108. The convex service-call signal pushes 997 up; the usage ramp 4397 shuts it for anyone with average or higher day usage. Mean contribution: 0 for 0-2 calls at any usage; at 3 calls +1.25 logit below 150 day minutes, +0.6 at 150-180; at 4 calls +4.0 / +2.6 / +0.9 (below 150 / 150-180 / 180-200 minutes); at 5 calls +7.0 / +4.4 / +2.6; at 6+ calls +10.7 / +8.5 / +5.5; about 0 above 220 minutes except for 6+ calls. Train churn with 4+ calls and under 150 day minutes is 87-100% (86 rows) vs 4-6% for 0-3 calls. Rare-state switches inside the gate: state:35 removes the usage brake (via 20866), so 9 of its 87 rows with 3+ calls get +0.5 to +6.8 logit (only 3 of the 9 churned); state:46 lowers the service-call signal (via 10379), so its high-call rows lose up to 2 more logit. Evidence (train, local forward passes): replacing this child's logit contribution by its least-squares linear fit on its entries changes train AUC 0.9193 -> 0.8945 (linear-fit R^2 0.35); restoring it alone onto the fully linearised model (AUC 0.8303) gives 0.8939 (gain +0.064). Closed form from get_formula; sensitivity summary attached.

annotations.name: churn_model
annotations.hypothesis: Root: P(churn) = sigmoid(-1.348 + linear_backbone + heavy_day_eve_usage + service_call_gate + day_charge_no_voicemail + csc_hinge + eve_charge_brake + state_offsets), additive in logit; the top-level children never feed each other (the heavy-usage hinge 1694 is split, with copy 1694_b inside the gate). The output also reads csc_escalation.10379 (the state:46 unit, grandchild exit) with weight -0.005. 30 unconnected inputs are zero-effect entries. Evidence (train, 4000 rows, local in-memory forward passes): full AUC 0.9193; all nonlinear children replaced by least-squares linear fits on their entries 0.8303 (jointly 0.8297; refit L2 logistic regression 0.8433). Restoring one child's nonlinearity alone onto the linearised model gains: service_call_gate +0.064, day_charge_no_voicemail +0.046, heavy_day_eve_usage +0.045, csc_hinge +0.007, eve_charge_brake -0.002. Shapley split of the gain: gate 0.041, day-charge 0.023, heavy-usage 0.022. Removing all state effects drops AUC to 0.9094 (0.010). SHAP top features: day minutes/charge, service calls, international plan, voicemail, eve charge.
